prompts: A policy newsletter is running a piece on which of Brazil's anti-inflation plans delivered what it promised, and wants a ranking it can defend. Research the plans in {WS}/RUBRIC.md on the open web: this one needs public sources, and you are allowed to browse. Score every plan with that rubric, rank the top 3, and write a one-page dossier for the editor in {WS}/dossier.md. Every number must carry the URL it came from. Record the result in {WS}/result.json: plans (one entry per plan with plan, launch_date, ipca_before, ipca_after, months_lasted, score and sources, a list of URLs) and top3 (plan names, best first).
answers:
[goal] Rank the six plans in RUBRIC.md and write `dossier.md` and `result.json`.

[action] I pulled IBGE's monthly IPCA from the Central Bank's series 433 (api.bcb.gov.br) and compounded each calendar year myself. All 12 months were present for every year from 1985 to 1996. I took launch dates from Wikipedia's timeline of the plans and the Collor II date from IDEC. I scored each plan with the rubric formula.

[result]
- Top 3, best first: **Real (0.994), Collor I (0.582), Collor II (0.422)**.
- The other three scored Bresser 0.095, Cruzado 0.075 and Verão 0.070.
- Annual IPCA (%) used for the plans: 1985 242.25, 1986 79.66, 1987 363.41, 1988 980.22, 1989 1972.91, 1990 1620.97, 1991 472.69, 1992 1119.09, 1993 2477.15, 1995 22.41. The dossier table gives the before/after pair for each plan.
- Both files were written by script. I did not re-open `result.json` afterwards.

How I know it's right:
- Cross-check: the 1995 figure (22.41%) and the 1996 figure (9.56%) match the Numerando IPCA table and the earlier search results.
- Not cross-checked: I found no second source for the 1985–1993 totals. Those rest on the Central Bank series alone.
- Unusable source: the IBGE PDF was a scanned image, so it gave me nothing.
- A site table showed 18.57% for 1994, but that table has no January–June data. The full series gives 916.43%. The rubric doesn't use 1994 in any score.

Assumptions:
- "Annual IPCA" means the compounded January–December rate.
- Months lasted counts whole months and respects the day of the month. That gives Cruzado 15, Bresser 19, Verão 14, Collor I 10, Collor II 41, and Real 60 as the rubric prescribes.
- Collor II launched on 31 January 1991. Sources differ between announcement and legal effect, but 1 February gives the same 41 months.
- The Wikipedia timeline lists no separate Collor II date, so that date rests on IDEC alone.

[next] The editor can add a second source for the pre-1994 IPCA, such as IBGE's SIDRA database, before publishing. Collor I ranks second on a big drop from the 1989 peak, not on how long it lasted (10 months).

--- dossier.md ---
# Dossier: which Brazilian anti-inflation plans delivered

Ranking (rubric in RUBRIC.md): **1. Real (0.994), 2. Collor I (0.582), 3. Collor II (0.422)**.

Annual IPCA (%) = 12 monthly IBGE rates compounded, from BCB series 433
(https://api.bcb.gov.br/dados/serie/bcdata.sgs.433/dados?formato=json&dataInicial=01/01/1985&dataFinal=31/12/1996).
Launch dates: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Brazilian_economic_stabilization_plans ; Collor II (31 Jan 1991): https://idec.org.br/em-acao/em-foco/prazo-para-entrar-com-acoes-do-plano-collor-ii-esta-se-esgotando

| Plan | Launch | IPCA before | IPCA after | Months | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cruzado | 1986-02-28 | 242.25 (1985) | 363.41 (1987) | 15 | 0.075 |
| Bresser | 1987-06-12 | 79.66 (1986) | 980.22 (1988) | 19 | 0.095 |
| Verao | 1989-01-15 | 980.22 (1988) | 1620.97 (1990) | 14 | 0.070 |
| Collor I | 1990-03-15 | 1972.91 (1989) | 472.69 (1991) | 10 | 0.582 |
| Collor II | 1991-01-31 | 1620.97 (1990) | 1119.09 (1992) | 41 | 0.422 |
| Real | 1994-07-01 | 2477.15 (1993) | 22.41 (1995) | 60 | 0.994 |

All figures above: BCB URL (inflation) and the Wikipedia/IDEC URLs (dates). 1995 = 22.41 and 1996 = 9.56 also match https://numerando.com.br/indices/ipca/tabela-completa.

Assumptions: "annual IPCA" is the Dec-to-Dec compounded monthly series; pre-1994 IPCA is the IBGE series as republished by BCB. Months = whole months, day-of-month respected (Collor II 31 Jan to 1 Jul 1994 = 41). Real uses 60 per rubric.
Caveats: Collor II's date differs across sources (announcement vs. MP 294 in force); using 1 Feb would still give 41 months. Collor I scores on a large drop from a very high 1989 base, not on durability (10 months).
